subject: lavPredict question regarding the method and local item dependence

messages.author: 7eff2529ffa05228
messages.subject: lavPredict question regarding the method and local item dependence
parts:
Hello,

I am using the lavPredict function for the following model: 


factor1=~ASBH20A+ASBH20B+ASBH17A+ASBH17B+ASBG04+ASDG05S+ASBH15A
#residual correlations
ASBH20A ~~ ASBH20B # to account for local item dependence
ASBH17A ~~ ASBH17B

fit <- cfa(mod, data = prePIRLS_2011, missing = "ML", sampling.weights = "TOTWGT", estimator = "ML")
lavPredict(fit, method = "ML")


Now I have two questions regarding the predict function: 
(1) The factor scores for the method "ML" are the same for the method "Bartlett"? I found in a paper* that it is recommend with high amount of missing values to use the "full ML approach" - what exactly is lavaan doing (does it estiamte the likelihood of the factors scores given the estiamtes of the CFA)?
(2) Is the interpretation of factor scores influenced by accounting for local item dependence (residual correlations)?


Friendly regards and thank you in advance
Julius Fenn



*Estabrook, R., & Neale, M. (2013). A comparison of factor score estimation methods in the presence of missing data: Reliability and an application to nicotine dependence. Multivariate behavioral research, 48(1), 1-27.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavPredict question regarding the method and local item dependence
parts: (2) Is the interpretation of factor scores influenced by accounting for local item dependence (residual correlations)?

It should make them more valid, because the common-factor variance (and any factor correlations) won't be overestimated by including specific-factor variance from any items that share another common cause.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavPredict question regarding the method and local item dependence
parts: > Now I have *two questions* regarding the predict function:

> (1) The factor scores for the method "ML" are the same for the
> method "Bartlett"?

When data is continuous, Bartlett == ML. In the presense of missing
data, lavaan (0.6-4) uses the equivalent of 'FIML' to compute the factor
scores (all available information is used). A new 'factor score matrix'
is computed for each missing pattern.

> (2) Is the interpretation of factor scores influenced by accounting
> for local item dependence (residual correlations)?

Yes. The standard formulas for both 'regression' and 'Bartlett' type
factor scores use (the inverse of) the full 'theta' matrix, when
computing the factor score matrix.

Yves.
